x <- read.delim("data/Gide_log2TPM.txt", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)

cat("int-like:", all(x==round(x)), "\n")
s <- colSums(2^x-1); cat("colSums(2^x-1):\n"); print(summary(s))
cat("dup genes:", sum(duplicated(rownames(x))), "\n")
cd <- read.table("data/colData_all.txt", header=TRUE, check.names=FALSE)

cat("cols in colData:", sum(colnames(x) %in% g$rna_id), "of", ncol(x), "\n")
print(setdiff(colnames(x), g$rna_id))
'

input.command:
mkdir -p results/input && Rscript -e '
x <- read.delim("data/Gide_log2TPM.txt", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
tpm <- 2^x - 1; tpm[tpm<0] <- 0
s <- sort(colSums(tpm)); print(head(s,5))
lo <- names(s)[1]; cat("genes >0 in", lo, ":", sum(tpm[,lo]>0), " median others:", median(colSums(tpm>0)), "\n")
write.csv(tpm, "results/input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv", quote=FALSE)
cd <- read.table("data/colData_all.txt", header=TRUE, check.names=FALSE)
g <- cd[cd$Cohort=="Gide", c("rna_id","Response","Therapy","Timing")]; rownames(g) <- g$rna_id
write.csv(g[colnames(tpm), -1], "results/input/Gide_coldata.csv", quote=FALSE)
'
head -c 300 results/input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv; echo; head -3 results/input/Gide_coldata.csv

content.text:
I've checked the data and prepared the inputs. I need two answers from you before I run the deconvolution.

**What I found:**
- `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` has 18,979 genes × 73 samples. Values run from 0 to 14, none are negative and none are whole numbers, so it's **log2(TPM+1)**. Deconvolution has to run on linear TPM, so I converted it back with 2^x − 1 and saved it as `results/input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`. That file will go to `run_deconvolution` with `normalized=False`.
- After converting back, each sample adds up to about 0.4–0.7 million rather than 1 million. That fits a gene subset of about 19k genes. One sample, `8_PD1_PRE`, is much lower at about 41k. It still has a normal number of detected genes, so I'll keep it, but I'll mark its results as less reliable.
- All 73 samples match the Gide rows in `colData_all.txt`. All are pre-treatment: 46 responders and 27 non-responders, with 44 on PD1 and 29 on ipi+PD1. I saved this as `results/input/Gide_coldata.csv`.

**Questions:**

1. **CIBERSORTx (CBSX):** CBSX is one of the 5 default methods, along with Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq and DWLS. It needs a CIBERSORTx account.
   - If you have one, send me your **email and API token**.
   - If you don't, you can register for free at https://cibersortx.stanford.edu. You can then either:
     - **(a)** run now without CBSX, using the other 4 methods, or
     - **(b)** wait until you have the credentials.

2. **Custom signatures:** Do you have your own signature matrix files (.txt) you want to use alongside the built-in ones, for example a melanoma-specific reference? If so, tell me where they are.

Once you reply, I'll run the deconvolution and then combine the methods into consensus cell subgroups. From those I'll calculate an immune infiltration score (total immune fraction and the main lymphoid and myeloid cell types) and a stromal score (fibroblasts and endothelial cells). Then I'll rank the patients and compare responders with non-responders. All of it will be saved in `results/`.

field_glossary.Deconvolution matrix: The harmonized cell-type proportion matrix after merging agreeing method/signature estimates into subgroups and removing zero-heavy/low-variance features -- this is the main output to carry into downstream analysis (for example pipeML-server, CellTFusion-server, RaCInG-server).
field_glossary.Deconvolution subgroups per cell types: For each canonical cell type, its final features: one column per subgroup (<CellType>_Subgroup.<i>, the median of its member features) plus the method/signature features that didn't group with any other.
field_glossary.Deconvolution subgroups composition: The subgroup membership structure itself: per cell type, which method/signature features make up each <CellType>_Subgroup.<i> (every pair of them correlates >= corr). This is the object replicate_subgroups and relate_subgroups_to_pathways expect as their subgroups/deconv_res input -- pass this call's run_dir/result.rds to those tools' *_rds parameter.
field_glossary.Discarded features with high number of z: Features dropped for exceeding zero_thr fraction of samples at zero -- usually a cell type this cohort's data can't reliably distinguish from absent.
field_glossary.Discarded features with low variance: Features dropped for near-constant values across samples (coefficient of variation, sd/mean, below cv_thr) -- uninformative for distinguishing samples from each other.
field_glossary.Discarded cell types: Cell type labels found in the input that aren't part of multideconv's standard nomenclature and weren't listed in cells_extra -- pass them via cells_extra if they're real, meaningful cell types you want kept.

content.text: The harmonization produced 222 features. Next I'll look at how the Immune, Stromal and key cell-type subgroups are composed, so I can build a robust infiltration score.

input.command:
Rscript -e '
r <- readRDS("results/03_harmonized_subgroups/result.rds")
comp <- r[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
for (ct in c("Immune","Lymphocytes","Myeloid.cells","Stromal","Cancer","CD8.cells","CAF","Fibroblasts","Endothelial","Macrophages.cells","Macrophages.M2","CD4.cells","B.cells")) { cat("==", ct, "==\n"); print(comp[[ct]]); cat("final cols:", colnames(r[["Deconvolution subgroups per cell types"]][[ct]]), "\n\n") }
' 2>&1 | head -150

Now writing the downstream analysis script.

input.content:
# Immune / stromal characterization of the Gide cohort from multideconv harmonized subgroups.
# Input : results/03_harmonized_subgroups (analyze_deconvolution) + results/input/Gide_coldata.csv
# Output: results/04_immune_stromal_summary/
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggpubr)
  library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize); library(patchwork)
})
set.seed(123)
base <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b329c858ac/work/results"
out  <- file.path(base, "04_immune_stromal_summary"); dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)

m  <- read.csv(file.path(base, "03_harmonized_subgroups/result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv"),
               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(m) <- sub("^X", "", rownames(m))          # R added an 'X' prefix to sample names
cd <- read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_coldata.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(rownames(m) %in% rownames(cd)))
cd <- cd[rownames(m), ]

# ---- Compartment scores ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only signatures that also model non-immune cells (HNSCC, Melanoma, Vanderbilt scRNAseq,
# and quanTIseq through its 'uncharacterized' fraction) give a true total immune fraction.
pct  <- function(x) rank(x, ties.method = "average") / length(x)   # within-cohort percentile
cons <- function(df) rowMeans(apply(df, 2, pct))                   # consensus = mean percentile
feat <- list(
  Immune      = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Immune", paste0("Immune_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  Lymphocytes = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Lymphocytes", "Lymphocytes_Subgroup.1",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.HNSCC.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Melanoma.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes"),
  Myeloid     = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Myeloid.cells", "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.1",
                  "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.2", grep("Macrophages.cells_Subgroup", colnames(m), value = TRUE)),
  Stromal     = c("DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Stromal", paste0("Stromal_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  Cancer      = grep("Cancer", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  CD8         = grep("^CD8.cells_Subgroup|_CD8.cells$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  CAF         = grep("^CAF_|_CAF$|^Fibroblasts_|_Fibroblasts$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  Endothelial = grep("^Endothelial_|_Endothelial$", colnames(m), value = TRUE)
)
feat <- lapply(feat, function(f) intersect(f, colnames(m)))
sink(file.path(out, "compartment_feature_definitions.txt"))

for (n in names(feat)) cat(n, ":\n  ", paste(feat[[n]], collapse = "\n   "), "\n\n")
sink()

scores <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(m))
for (n in names(feat)) {
  scores[[paste0(n, "_score")]]   <- cons(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE])
  scores[[paste0(n, "_fraction")]] <- apply(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE], 1, median)
}
# Per-estimate agreement of the immune and stromal features
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Immune], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "immune_estimates_spearman.csv"))
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Stromal], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "stromal_estimates_spearman.csv"))

# ---- Patient classification --------------------------------------------------------------
q <- quantile(scores$Immune_score, c(1/3, 2/3))
scores$Immune_class <- cut(scores$Immune_score, c(-Inf, q, Inf),
                           labels = c("Immune-low", "Immune-intermediate", "Immune-high"))
scores$TME_class <- paste0(ifelse(scores$Immune_score  >= median(scores$Immune_score),  "Immune-high", "Immune-low"), " / ",
                           ifelse(scores$Stromal_score >= median(scores$Stromal_score), "Stroma-high", "Stroma-low"))
scores$Immune_rank <- rank(-scores$Immune_score, ties.method = "min")
# QC flag: very low library-equivalent TPM total (see 00 input checks)
tpm_tot <- colSums(read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
scores$TPM_total <- round(tpm_tot[rownames(scores)])
scores$QC_flag <- ifelse(scores$TPM_total < 0.25 * median(tpm_tot), "low total TPM - interpret with caution", "")

res <- cbind(Sample = rownames(scores), cd[rownames(scores), c("Response", "Therapy")], scores)
res <- res[order(res$Immune_rank), ]
num <- sapply(res, is.numeric) & !names(res) %in% c("Immune_rank", "TPM_total")
res[num] <- lapply(res[num], round, 4)
write.csv(res, file.path(out, "patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Association with clinical variables -------------------------------------------------
test_vars <- grep("_score$", colnames(scores), value = TRUE)
assoc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Response", "Therapy"), function(v) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(test_vars, function(s) {
    g <- cd[[v]]; lv <- sort(unique(g))
    w <- wilcox.test(scores[[s]] ~ g)
    data.frame(variable = v, score = s,
               group1 = lv[1], median1 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[1]]),
               group2 = lv[2], median2 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[2]]), p = w$p.value)
  }))
}))
assoc$padj_BH <- ave(assoc$p, assoc$variable, FUN = function(p) p.adjust(p, "BH"))
write.csv(assoc, file.path(out, "compartment_scores_vs_clinical_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

tab <- table(scores$Immune_class, cd$Response)
fis <- fisher.test(tab)
sink(file.path(out, "immune_class_vs_response.txt"))
print(tab); cat("\nFisher's exact test p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response)); cat("\nFisher p =", signif(fisher.test(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response))$p.value, 3), "\n")
sink()

# All harmonized features vs response (exploratory, BH-corrected)
fr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(colnames(m), function(f) {
  data.frame(feature = f, median_NR = median(m[cd$Response == "NR", f]), median_R = median(m[cd$Response == "R", f]),
             p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(m[, f] ~ cd$Response)$p.value))
}))
fr$padj_BH <- p.adjust(fr$p, "BH"); fr <- fr[order(fr$p), ]
write.csv(fr, file.path(out, "all_harmonized_features_vs_response_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ord <- rownames(scores)[order(scores$Immune_score, decreasing = TRUE)]
# 1. Ranked immune score with response
p1 <- ggplot(res, aes(x = reorder(Sample, -Immune_score), y = Immune_score, fill = Immune_class)) +
  geom_col() + geom_point(aes(y = -0.04, shape = Response), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Consensus immune score (mean percentile)", title = "Gide cohort: ranked immune infiltration") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_score_ranked.pdf"), p1, width = 14, height = 5)

# 2. Stacked compartment composition (median absolute fraction, renormalized to 1)
comp <- scores[, c("Lymphocytes_fraction", "Myeloid_fraction", "Stromal_fraction", "Cancer_fraction")]
comp$Other <- pmax(0, 1 - rowSums(comp)); comp <- comp / rowSums(comp)
cl <- comp %>% mutate(Sample = rownames(comp)) %>% pivot_longer(-Sample, names_to = "Compartment", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = ord), Compartment = sub("_fraction", "", Compartment))
p2 <- ggplot(cl, aes(Sample, Fraction, fill = Compartment)) + geom_col(width = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Lymphocytes = "#d73027", Myeloid = "#fc8d59", Stromal = "#1a9850", Cancer = "#762a83", Other = "grey80")) +
  labs(x = "Samples (ordered by immune score)", y = "Relative fraction",
       title = "Compartment composition (median across references, renormalized)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_composition_stacked.pdf"), p2, width = 14, height = 5)

# 3. Immune vs stromal scatter
p3 <- ggplot(res, aes(Stromal_score, Immune_score, colour = Response, shape = Therapy)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(res$Stromal_score), lty = 2) + geom_hline(yintercept = median(res$Immune_score), lty = 2) +
  stat_cor(aes(group = 1), method = "spearman", colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal consensus scores") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_vs_stromal_scatter.pdf"), p3, width = 7, height = 6)

# 4. Scores by response
long <- res %>% select(Sample, Response, all_of(test_vars)) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(test_vars), names_to = "Score") %>%
  mutate(Score = sub("_score", "", Score))
p4 <- ggplot(long, aes(Response, value, fill = Response)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = .6) +
  geom_jitter(width = .15, size = 1) + facet_wrap(~Score, nrow = 2) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label = "p.format", label.x = 1.3) +
  labs(y = "Consensus score (mean percentile)", title = "Compartment scores by response") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_scores_by_response.pdf"), p4, width = 11, height = 6)

# 5. Heatmap of harmonized cell-type features (scaled), samples ordered by immune score
mat <- t(scale(m[ord, ])); mat[mat > 3] <- 3; mat[mat < -3] <- -3
ct <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", rownames(mat)); ct <- ifelse(grepl("_", ct), sub(".*_", "", ct), ct)
top <- HeatmapAnnotation(Immune_score = scores[ord, "Immune_score"], Stromal_score = scores[ord, "Stromal_score"],
                         Immune_class = scores[ord, "Immune_class"], Response = cd[ord, "Response"], Therapy = cd[ord, "Therapy"],
                         col = list(Immune_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#d73027")),
                                    Stromal_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#1a9850")),
                                    Immune_class = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027"),
                                    Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
                                    Therapy = c(PD1 = "#7570b3", "CTLA4+PD1" = "#e7298a")))
pdf(file.path(out, "harmonized_features_heatmap.pdf"), width = 16, height = 30)
draw(Heatmap(mat, name = "z", top_annotation = top, cluster_columns = FALSE, row_split = ct, row_title_rot = 0,
             row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7), row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 5), column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
             cluster_row_slices = FALSE, col = colorRamp2(c(-3, 0, 3), c("#4575b4", "white", "#d73027"))))
dev.off()

# Console summary
cat("Immune class x response:\n"); print(tab); cat("Fisher p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(assoc, digits = 3)
cat("\nTop 10 immune-infiltrated:\n"); print(head(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nBottom 10:\n"); print(tail(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nTop features vs response:\n"); print(head(fr, 15), digits = 3)
cat("\nQC flagged:\n"); print(res[res$QC_flag != "", c("Sample", "Immune_rank", "TPM_total")])

# Immune / stromal characterization of the Gide cohort from multideconv harmonized subgroups.
# Input : results/03_harmonized_subgroups (analyze_deconvolution) + results/input/Gide_coldata.csv
# Output: results/04_immune_stromal_summary/
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggpubr)
  library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize); library(patchwork)
})
set.seed(123)
base <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b329c858ac/work/results"
out  <- file.path(base, "04_immune_stromal_summary"); dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)

m  <- read.csv(file.path(base, "03_harmonized_subgroups/result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv"),
               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(m) <- sub("^X", "", rownames(m))          # R added an 'X' prefix to sample names
cd <- read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_coldata.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(rownames(m) %in% rownames(cd)))
cd <- cd[rownames(m), ]

# ---- Compartment scores ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only signatures that also model non-immune cells (HNSCC, Melanoma, Vanderbilt scRNAseq,
# and quanTIseq through its 'uncharacterized' fraction) give a true total immune fraction.
pct  <- function(x) rank(x, ties.method = "average") / length(x)   # within-cohort percentile
cons <- function(df) rowMeans(apply(df, 2, pct))                   # consensus = mean percentile
feat <- list(
  Immune      = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Immune", paste0("Immune_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  Lymphocytes = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Lymphocytes", "Lymphocytes_Subgroup.1",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.HNSCC.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Melanoma.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes"),
  Myeloid     = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Myeloid.cells", "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.1",
                  "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.2", grep("Macrophages.cells_Subgroup", colnames(m), value = TRUE)),
  Stromal     = c("DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Stromal", paste0("Stromal_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  Cancer      = grep("Cancer", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  CD8         = grep("^CD8.cells_Subgroup|_CD8.cells$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  CAF         = grep("^CAF_|_CAF$|^Fibroblasts_|_Fibroblasts$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  Endothelial = grep("^Endothelial_|_Endothelial$", colnames(m), value = TRUE)
)
feat <- lapply(feat, function(f) intersect(f, colnames(m)))
sink(file.path(out, "compartment_feature_definitions.txt"))
for (n in names(feat)) cat(n, ":\n  ", paste(feat[[n]], collapse = "\n   "), "\n\n")
sink()

scores <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(m))
for (n in names(feat)) {
  scores[[paste0(n, "_score")]]   <- cons(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE])
  scores[[paste0(n, "_fraction")]] <- apply(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE], 1, median)
}
# Per-estimate agreement of the immune and stromal features
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Immune], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "immune_estimates_spearman.csv"))
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Stromal], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "stromal_estimates_spearman.csv"))

# ---- Patient classification --------------------------------------------------------------
q <- quantile(scores$Immune_score, c(1/3, 2/3))
scores$Immune_class <- cut(scores$Immune_score, c(-Inf, q, Inf),
                           labels = c("Immune-low", "Immune-intermediate", "Immune-high"))
scores$TME_class <- paste0(ifelse(scores$Immune_score  >= median(scores$Immune_score),  "Immune-high", "Immune-low"), " / ",
                           ifelse(scores$Stromal_score >= median(scores$Stromal_score), "Stroma-high", "Stroma-low"))
scores$Immune_rank <- rank(-scores$Immune_score, ties.method = "min")
# QC flag: very low library-equivalent TPM total (see 00 input checks)
tpm_tot <- colSums(read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
scores$TPM_total <- round(tpm_tot[rownames(scores)])
scores$QC_flag <- ifelse(scores$TPM_total < 0.25 * median(tpm_tot), "low total TPM - interpret with caution", "")

res <- cbind(Sample = rownames(scores), cd[rownames(scores), c("Response", "Therapy")], scores)
res <- res[order(res$Immune_rank), ]
num <- sapply(res, is.numeric) & !names(res) %in% c("Immune_rank", "TPM_total")
res[num] <- lapply(res[num], round, 4)
write.csv(res, file.path(out, "patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Association with clinical variables -------------------------------------------------
test_vars <- grep("_score$", colnames(scores), value = TRUE)
assoc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Response", "Therapy"), function(v) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(test_vars, function(s) {
    g <- cd[[v]]; lv <- sort(unique(g))
    w <- wilcox.test(scores[[s]] ~ g)
    data.frame(variable = v, score = s,
               group1 = lv[1], median1 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[1]]),
               group2 = lv[2], median2 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[2]]), p = w$p.value)
  }))
}))
assoc$padj_BH <- ave(assoc$p, assoc$variable, FUN = function(p) p.adjust(p, "BH"))
write.csv(assoc, file.path(out, "compartment_scores_vs_clinical_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

tab <- table(scores$Immune_class, cd$Response)
fis <- fisher.test(tab)
sink(file.path(out, "immune_class_vs_response.txt"))
print(tab); cat("\nFisher's exact test p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response)); cat("\nFisher p =", signif(fisher.test(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response))$p.value, 3), "\n")
sink()

# All harmonized features vs response (exploratory, BH-corrected)
fr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(colnames(m), function(f) {
  data.frame(feature = f, median_NR = median(m[cd$Response == "NR", f]), median_R = median(m[cd$Response == "R", f]),
             p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(m[, f] ~ cd$Response)$p.value))
}))
fr$padj_BH <- p.adjust(fr$p, "BH"); fr <- fr[order(fr$p), ]
write.csv(fr, file.path(out, "all_harmonized_features_vs_response_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ord <- rownames(scores)[order(scores$Immune_score, decreasing = TRUE)]
# 1. Ranked immune score with response
p1 <- ggplot(res, aes(x = reorder(Sample, -Immune_score), y = Immune_score, fill = Immune_class)) +
  geom_col() + geom_point(aes(y = -0.04, shape = Response), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Consensus immune score (mean percentile)", title = "Gide cohort: ranked immune infiltration") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_score_ranked.pdf"), p1, width = 14, height = 5)

# 2. Stacked compartment composition (median absolute fraction, renormalized to 1)
comp <- scores[, c("Lymphocytes_fraction", "Myeloid_fraction", "Stromal_fraction", "Cancer_fraction")]
comp$Other <- pmax(0, 1 - rowSums(comp)); comp <- comp / rowSums(comp)
cl <- comp %>% mutate(Sample = rownames(comp)) %>% pivot_longer(-Sample, names_to = "Compartment", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = ord), Compartment = sub("_fraction", "", Compartment))
p2 <- ggplot(cl, aes(Sample, Fraction, fill = Compartment)) + geom_col(width = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Lymphocytes = "#d73027", Myeloid = "#fc8d59", Stromal = "#1a9850", Cancer = "#762a83", Other = "grey80")) +
  labs(x = "Samples (ordered by immune score)", y = "Relative fraction",
       title = "Compartment composition (median across references, renormalized)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_composition_stacked.pdf"), p2, width = 14, height = 5)

# 3. Immune vs stromal scatter
p3 <- ggplot(res, aes(Stromal_score, Immune_score, colour = Response, shape = Therapy)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(res$Stromal_score), lty = 2) + geom_hline(yintercept = median(res$Immune_score), lty = 2) +
  stat_cor(aes(group = 1), method = "spearman", colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal consensus scores") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_vs_stromal_scatter.pdf"), p3, width = 7, height = 6)

# 4. Scores by response
long <- res %>% select(Sample, Response, all_of(test_vars)) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(test_vars), names_to = "Score") %>%
  mutate(Score = sub("_score", "", Score))
p4 <- ggplot(long, aes(Response, value, fill = Response)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = .6) +
  geom_jitter(width = .15, size = 1) + facet_wrap(~Score, nrow = 2) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label = "p.format", label.x = 1.3) +
  labs(y = "Consensus score (mean percentile)", title = "Compartment scores by response") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_scores_by_response.pdf"), p4, width = 11, height = 6)

# 5. Heatmap of harmonized cell-type features (scaled), samples ordered by immune score
mat <- t(scale(m[ord, ])); mat[mat > 3] <- 3; mat[mat < -3] <- -3
ct <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", rownames(mat)); ct <- ifelse(grepl("_", ct), sub(".*_", "", ct), ct)
top <- HeatmapAnnotation(Immune_score = scores[ord, "Immune_score"], Stromal_score = scores[ord, "Stromal_score"],
                         Immune_class = scores[ord, "Immune_class"], Response = cd[ord, "Response"], Therapy = cd[ord, "Therapy"],
                         col = list(Immune_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#d73027")),
                                    Stromal_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#1a9850")),
                                    Immune_class = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027"),
                                    Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
                                    Therapy = c(PD1 = "#7570b3", "CTLA4+PD1" = "#e7298a")))
pdf(file.path(out, "harmonized_features_heatmap.pdf"), width = 16, height = 30)
draw(Heatmap(mat, name = "z", top_annotation = top, cluster_columns = FALSE, row_split = ct, row_title_rot = 0,
             row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7), row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 5), column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
             cluster_row_slices = FALSE, col = colorRamp2(c(-3, 0, 3), c("#4575b4", "white", "#d73027"))))
dev.off()

# Console summary
cat("Immune class x response:\n"); print(tab); cat("Fisher p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(assoc, digits = 3)
cat("\nTop 10 immune-infiltrated:\n"); print(head(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nBottom 10:\n"); print(tail(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nTop features vs response:\n"); print(head(fr, 15), digits = 3)
cat("\nQC flagged:\n"); print(res[res$QC_flag != "", c("Sample", "Immune_rank", "TPM_total")])

# Immune / stromal characterization of the Gide cohort from multideconv harmonized subgroups.
# Input : results/03_harmonized_subgroups (analyze_deconvolution) + results/input/Gide_coldata.csv
# Output: results/04_immune_stromal_summary/
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggpubr)
  library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize); library(patchwork)
})
set.seed(123)
base <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b329c858ac/work/results"
out  <- file.path(base, "04_immune_stromal_summary"); dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)

m  <- read.csv(file.path(base, "03_harmonized_subgroups/result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv"),
               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(m) <- sub("^X", "", rownames(m))          # R added an 'X' prefix to sample names
cd <- read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_coldata.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(rownames(m) %in% rownames(cd)))
cd <- cd[rownames(m), ]

# ---- Compartment scores ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only signatures that also model non-immune cells (HNSCC, Melanoma, Vanderbilt scRNAseq,
# and quanTIseq through its 'uncharacterized' fraction) give a true total immune fraction.
pct  <- function(x) rank(x, ties.method = "average") / length(x)   # within-cohort percentile
cons <- function(df) rowMeans(apply(df, 2, pct))                   # consensus = mean percentile
feat <- list(
  Immune      = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Immune", paste0("Immune_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  Lymphocytes = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Lymphocytes", "Lymphocytes_Subgroup.1",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.HNSCC.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Melanoma.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes",
                  "DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Lymphocytes"),
  Myeloid     = c("Quantiseq_TIL10_Myeloid.cells", "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.1",
                  "Myeloid.cells_Subgroup.2", grep("Macrophages.cells_Subgroup", colnames(m), value = TRUE)),
  Stromal     = c("DeconRNASeq_CBSX.Vanderbilt.scRNAseq_Stromal", paste0("Stromal_Subgroup.", 1:3)),
  # HNSCC/Vanderbilt 'Cancer' profiles are non-melanocytic tumour cells (~0 in melanoma);
  # keep only the melanoma-reference subgroup (CBSX.Melanoma.scRNAseq, 4 methods)
  Cancer      = "Cancer_Subgroup.2",
  CD8         = grep("^CD8.cells_Subgroup|_CD8.cells$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  CAF         = grep("^CAF_|_CAF$|^Fibroblasts_|_Fibroblasts$", colnames(m), value = TRUE),
  Endothelial = grep("^Endothelial_|_Endothelial$", colnames(m), value = TRUE)
)
feat <- lapply(feat, function(f) intersect(f, colnames(m)))
sink(file.path(out, "compartment_feature_definitions.txt"))
for (n in names(feat)) cat(n, ":\n  ", paste(feat[[n]], collapse = "\n   "), "\n\n")
sink()

scores <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(m))
for (n in names(feat)) {
  scores[[paste0(n, "_score")]]   <- cons(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE])
  scores[[paste0(n, "_fraction")]] <- apply(m[, feat[[n]], drop = FALSE], 1, median)
}
# Per-estimate agreement of the immune and stromal features
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Immune], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "immune_estimates_spearman.csv"))
write.csv(round(cor(m[, feat$Stromal], method = "spearman"), 3), file.path(out, "stromal_estimates_spearman.csv"))

# ---- Patient classification --------------------------------------------------------------
q <- quantile(scores$Immune_score, c(1/3, 2/3))
scores$Immune_class <- cut(scores$Immune_score, c(-Inf, q, Inf),
                           labels = c("Immune-low", "Immune-intermediate", "Immune-high"))
scores$TME_class <- paste0(ifelse(scores$Immune_score  >= median(scores$Immune_score),  "Immune-high", "Immune-low"), " / ",
                           ifelse(scores$Stromal_score >= median(scores$Stromal_score), "Stroma-high", "Stroma-low"))
scores$Immune_rank <- rank(-scores$Immune_score, ties.method = "min")
# QC flag: very low library-equivalent TPM total (see 00 input checks)
tpm_tot <- colSums(read.csv(file.path(base, "input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
scores$TPM_total <- round(tpm_tot[rownames(scores)])
scores$QC_flag <- ifelse(scores$TPM_total < 0.25 * median(tpm_tot), "low total TPM - interpret with caution", "")

res <- cbind(Sample = rownames(scores), cd[rownames(scores), c("Response", "Therapy")], scores)
res <- res[order(res$Immune_rank), ]
num <- sapply(res, is.numeric) & !names(res) %in% c("Immune_rank", "TPM_total")
res[num] <- lapply(res[num], round, 4)
write.csv(res, file.path(out, "patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Association with clinical variables -------------------------------------------------
test_vars <- grep("_score$", colnames(scores), value = TRUE)
assoc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Response", "Therapy"), function(v) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(test_vars, function(s) {
    g <- cd[[v]]; lv <- sort(unique(g))
    w <- wilcox.test(scores[[s]] ~ g)
    data.frame(variable = v, score = s,
               group1 = lv[1], median1 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[1]]),
               group2 = lv[2], median2 = median(scores[[s]][g == lv[2]]), p = w$p.value)
  }))
}))
assoc$padj_BH <- ave(assoc$p, assoc$variable, FUN = function(p) p.adjust(p, "BH"))
write.csv(assoc, file.path(out, "compartment_scores_vs_clinical_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

tab <- table(scores$Immune_class, cd$Response)
fis <- fisher.test(tab)
sink(file.path(out, "immune_class_vs_response.txt"))
print(tab); cat("\nFisher's exact test p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response)); cat("\nFisher p =", signif(fisher.test(table(scores$TME_class, cd$Response))$p.value, 3), "\n")
sink()

# All harmonized features vs response (exploratory, BH-corrected)
fr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(colnames(m), function(f) {
  data.frame(feature = f, median_NR = median(m[cd$Response == "NR", f]), median_R = median(m[cd$Response == "R", f]),
             p = suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(m[, f] ~ cd$Response)$p.value))
}))
fr$padj_BH <- p.adjust(fr$p, "BH"); fr <- fr[order(fr$p), ]
write.csv(fr, file.path(out, "all_harmonized_features_vs_response_wilcoxon.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ord <- rownames(scores)[order(scores$Immune_score, decreasing = TRUE)]
# 1. Ranked immune score with response
p1 <- ggplot(res, aes(x = reorder(Sample, -Immune_score), y = Immune_score, fill = Immune_class)) +
  geom_col() + geom_point(aes(y = -0.04, shape = Response), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Consensus immune score (mean percentile)", title = "Gide cohort: ranked immune infiltration") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_score_ranked.pdf"), p1, width = 14, height = 5)

# 2. Stacked compartment composition (median absolute fraction, renormalized to 1)
comp <- scores[, c("Lymphocytes_fraction", "Myeloid_fraction", "Stromal_fraction", "Cancer_fraction")]
comp$Other <- pmax(0, 1 - rowSums(comp)); comp <- comp / rowSums(comp)
cl <- comp %>% mutate(Sample = rownames(comp)) %>% pivot_longer(-Sample, names_to = "Compartment", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = ord), Compartment = sub("_fraction", "", Compartment))
p2 <- ggplot(cl, aes(Sample, Fraction, fill = Compartment)) + geom_col(width = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Lymphocytes = "#d73027", Myeloid = "#fc8d59", Stromal = "#1a9850", Cancer = "#762a83", Other = "grey80")) +
  labs(x = "Samples (ordered by immune score)", y = "Relative fraction",
       title = "Compartment composition (median across references, renormalized)") +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6))
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_composition_stacked.pdf"), p2, width = 14, height = 5)

# 3. Immune vs stromal scatter
p3 <- ggplot(res, aes(Stromal_score, Immune_score, colour = Response, shape = Therapy)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(res$Stromal_score), lty = 2) + geom_hline(yintercept = median(res$Immune_score), lty = 2) +
  stat_cor(aes(group = 1), method = "spearman", colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal consensus scores") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "immune_vs_stromal_scatter.pdf"), p3, width = 7, height = 6)

# 4. Scores by response
long <- res %>% select(Sample, Response, all_of(test_vars)) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(test_vars), names_to = "Score") %>%
  mutate(Score = sub("_score", "", Score))
p4 <- ggplot(long, aes(Response, value, fill = Response)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = .6) +
  geom_jitter(width = .15, size = 1) + facet_wrap(~Score, nrow = 2) +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", label = "p.format", label.x = 1.3) +
  labs(y = "Consensus score (mean percentile)", title = "Compartment scores by response") + theme_bw()
ggsave(file.path(out, "compartment_scores_by_response.pdf"), p4, width = 11, height = 6)

# 5. Heatmap of harmonized cell-type features (scaled), samples ordered by immune score
mat <- t(scale(m[ord, ])); mat[mat > 3] <- 3; mat[mat < -3] <- -3
ct <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", rownames(mat)); ct <- ifelse(grepl("_", ct), sub(".*_", "", ct), ct)
top <- HeatmapAnnotation(Immune_score = scores[ord, "Immune_score"], Stromal_score = scores[ord, "Stromal_score"],
                         Immune_class = scores[ord, "Immune_class"], Response = cd[ord, "Response"], Therapy = cd[ord, "Therapy"],
                         col = list(Immune_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#d73027")),
                                    Stromal_score = colorRamp2(c(0, 1), c("white", "#1a9850")),
                                    Immune_class = c("Immune-low" = "#4575b4", "Immune-intermediate" = "#fee090", "Immune-high" = "#d73027"),
                                    Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
                                    Therapy = c(PD1 = "#7570b3", "CTLA4+PD1" = "#e7298a")))
pdf(file.path(out, "harmonized_features_heatmap.pdf"), width = 16, height = 30)
draw(Heatmap(mat, name = "z", top_annotation = top, cluster_columns = FALSE, row_split = ct, row_title_rot = 0,
             row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 7), row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 5), column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
             cluster_row_slices = FALSE, col = colorRamp2(c(-3, 0, 3), c("#4575b4", "white", "#d73027"))))
dev.off()

# Console summary
cat("Immune class x response:\n"); print(tab); cat("Fisher p =", signif(fis$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
print(assoc, digits = 3)
cat("\nTop 10 immune-infiltrated:\n"); print(head(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nBottom 10:\n"); print(tail(res[, c("Sample", "Response", "Therapy", "Immune_score", "Immune_fraction", "Stromal_score", "TME_class", "QC_flag")], 10))
cat("\nTop features vs response:\n"); print(head(fr, 15), digits = 3)
cat("\nQC flagged:\n"); print(res[res$QC_flag != "", c("Sample", "Immune_rank", "TPM_total")])

# Gide cohort – immune & stromal composition (multideconv)

73 pre-treatment melanoma samples (anti-PD1 n=44, ipi+PD1 n=29; R=46, NR=27).

## Input handling
- `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` holds log2(TPM+1) (range 0–14, non-negative, non-integer). Deconvolution needs linear TPM,
  so it was back-transformed (2^x − 1) → `input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`, passed to `run_deconvolution(normalized=FALSE)`.
- Clinical annotation (Gide rows of `colData_all.txt`) → `input/Gide_coldata.csv`.
- QC: `8_PD1_PRE` has a much lower TPM total (~41k vs ~510k median) – kept, flagged in the score table.

## Steps
| Folder | Tool | What |
|---|---|---|
| `01_deconvolution/` | multideconv `run_deconvolution` | Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS, CIBERSORTx × all bundled signatures → 29 method-signature combinations, 375 features |
| `02_aggregated_groups/` | `aggregate_cell_groups` | added Immune, Lymphocytes, Myeloid.cells, Stromal sums per combination |
| `03_harmonized_subgroups/` | `analyze_deconvolution` (corr 0.7, Spearman) | cross-method consensus subgroups → 222 features (`result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv`) |
| `04_immune_stromal_summary/` | `scripts/04_immune_stromal_summary.R` | compartment scores, patient classes, clinical association, figures |

## Scores (04_immune_stromal_summary)
- **Consensus score** per compartment = mean within-cohort percentile across the harmonized features of that compartment
  (definitions in `compartment_feature_definitions.txt`). Total-immune and stromal scores only use references that also model
  non-immune cells (quanTIseq, CBSX HNSCC / Melanoma / Vanderbilt scRNAseq signatures). `*_fraction` = median absolute estimate.
- Cancer score uses only the melanoma scRNAseq reference (HNSCC/Vanderbilt tumour profiles are non-melanocytic, ~0 here).
- **Immune_class**: tertiles of the immune score. **TME_class**: median splits of immune × stromal score.

## Key files
- `patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv` – per-patient scores, rank, classes, QC flag (sorted most → least infiltrated)
- `compartment_scores_vs_clinical_wilcoxon.csv`, `immune_class_vs_response.txt`, `all_harmonized_features_vs_response_wilcoxon.csv`
- Figures: `immune_score_ranked.pdf`, `compartment_composition_stacked.pdf`, `immune_vs_stromal_scatter.pdf`,
  `compartment_scores_by_response.pdf`, `harmonized_features_heatmap.pdf`
- `session_export/` – multideconv session reproducibility log

content.text:
## Gide cohort: immune and stromal composition

**The patients with the most immune infiltration are 20_ipiPD1_PRE, 13_ipiPD1_PRE, 7_PD1_PRE, 6_PD1_PRE, 37_ipiPD1_PRE, 45_PD1_PRE, 40_PD1_PRE, 44_PD1_PRE, 48_PD1_PRE and 53_PD1_PRE.** These are the top 10 of 24 patients I classed as immune-high (the top third). The full ranked list is in `results/04_immune_stromal_summary/patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv`.

**How I got there:**
- **Scale:** your file holds log2(TPM+1) values, so I converted them back to linear TPM before deconvolution.
- **Deconvolution:** all 5 methods ran (Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS, CIBERSORTx), giving 29 method–reference combinations. Before merging, I added total Immune, Lymphocyte, Myeloid and Stromal sums for each combination. Merging estimates that agree across methods left 222 cell-type features.
- **Immune score:** I combined 4 independent total-immune estimates by averaging each patient's rank within the cohort. The estimates agree moderately (Spearman 0.40–0.75), and their absolute levels differ between references, which is why I used ranks.
- **Stromal score:** built the same way from fibroblasts/CAFs, endothelial and mural cells.
- **Classes:** patients are split into thirds by immune score. A second classification combines immune and stromal scores, each split at the median.

**Immune and stromal content**

| Immune class | n | Median immune fraction | Responder / non-responder |
|---|---|---|---|
| Immune-high | 24 | 54% | 22 / 2 |
| Immune-intermediate | 23 | 37% | 12 / 11 |
| Immune-low | 26 | 22% | 12 / 14 |

- **Immune and stromal content move in opposite directions** (Spearman ρ = −0.61, p < 1e-8). Immune-high tumours contain CD8 and CD4 T cells, NK cells and macrophages. Immune-low tumours are mostly cancer cells and CAFs.
- **Tumour content:** the melanoma-specific reference puts the median tumour-cell fraction at 59%.
- **Immune-high with low stroma** is the class most enriched for responders: 21 of 24 responded (Fisher p = 0.018 across the four classes).

**Relation to response.** These are exploratory comparisons by Wilcoxon test, with Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjusted p-values:
- **CD8 T cells** separate responders from non-responders most clearly (adjusted p = 1e-4).
- **Total immune:** adjusted p = 0.019.
- **Lymphocytes:** adjusted p = 0.034.
- **Stromal, CAF and myeloid** scores are not significantly different.
- **Immune class against response:** Fisher p = 8e-4.
- **Therapy arm:** no compartment differs between PD1 and ipi+PD1 after correction.

**Things to be aware of:**
- **Outliers:** two non-responders, 7_PD1_PRE and 6_PD1_PRE, are among the most infiltrated tumours. A high immune fraction does not always mean an active immune response. Looking at the regulatory state of those cells, for example with CellTFusion, could explain these cases if you want to go further.
- **Low-total sample:** 8_PD1_PRE has a much lower total expression than the other samples. I kept it but flagged it in the score table. It ranks among the least infiltrated.
- **Cancer score:** I based it only on the melanoma reference. The HNSCC and Vanderbilt references model non-melanoma tumour cells and estimate almost none in these samples.
- **Credentials:** your CIBERSORTx token is stored in plain text in `results/01_deconvolution/manifest.json`. It is masked in the exported session log. I can remove it from the manifest if you plan to share the folder.

Everything is in `results/`, with a `README.md` describing each part:
- `input/`
- `01_deconvolution/`
- `02_aggregated_groups/`
- `03_harmonized_subgroups/`
- `04_immune_stromal_summary/` (scores, tests and figures)
- `scripts/`
- `session_export/` (session log)

content.text:
## 1. Input data

- **Transformation:** `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` held log2(TPM+1) values (range 0–14, non-negative, non-integer). I converted it to linear TPM with 2^x − 1 and clipped negatives to 0. The result is `results/input/Gide_TPM_linear.csv`.
- **Where it was used:**
  - As input to `run_deconvolution` (`normalized=FALSE`), because deconvolution needs linear TPM.
  - For the per-sample TPM totals used in the QC flag.
- **No renormalization:** I did not rescale samples to sum to 1e6. Each sample totals about 0.4–0.7M, presumably because the file holds only about 19k genes.
- **No log-scale step:** nothing in the analysis used the log2 values directly.
- **Sample names:** I removed the "X" prefix that R added to sample names, so they match the clinical table.

## 2. Methods

**Ran:**
- `start_workflow_session`
- `run_deconvolution` with Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS and CBSX, across all bundled signatures
- `aggregate_cell_groups`
- `analyze_deconvolution`
- `export_session_results`
- My own R script, `results/scripts/04_immune_stromal_summary.R`, which computes the consensus scores, classes, Wilcoxon and Fisher tests, and figures

**Skipped:**
- `benchmark_deconvolution`: there are no known cell fractions to compare against.
- `relate_subgroups_to_pathways`: you didn't ask for it, and it needs pathway activity.
- `replicate_subgroups`: you didn't ask for a second cohort. `Riaz_log2TPM.txt` is in `data/` but I didn't use it.
- CellTFusion: infiltration is a composition question.
- BioinfoTools `scores_stat_analysis_categorical`: I did the response and therapy tests in my own R script instead. That was a choice, not a requirement.

## 3. Non-default parameters

**`run_deconvolution`:**
- `normalized=FALSE`, because the input was linear TPM.
- CBSX credentials, read from your file.
- `workers=3`, after the first run used 19 workers and ran out of memory.
- `output_dir` and `file_name`.
- I listed the methods explicitly, but they are the same five as the default.

**`aggregate_cell_groups`:** I defined the groups myself:
- Immune included mast cells and eosinophils.
- Myeloid excluded mast cells and eosinophils.
- Lymphocytes included plasma cells.

**`analyze_deconvolution`:**
- `cells_extra = Immune, Lymphocytes, Stromal`.
- `Myeloid.cells` is already standard multideconv naming, so it was kept anyway.
- I left all other parameters at their defaults. The README says "corr 0.7, Spearman"; I did not check those defaults, so treat that as unverified.

**My own script:**
- Consensus score = mean of each patient's within-cohort percentile across that compartment's features.
- Immune classes are tertiles; the immune × stromal classes use median splits.
- QC flag for samples with a TPM total below 25% of the median.
- The Cancer score uses only `Cancer_Subgroup.2`, the melanoma reference.

All of these are my own choices, not established cutoffs.

## 4. Problems

- **Out-of-memory crash:** the first `run_deconvolution` was killed (exit −9) when DWLS started on 19 workers. The machine had 15 GB RAM with about 5 GB free. I reran with 3 workers, and it completed.
- **Cancer score:** I first used all "Cancer" features. The HNSCC and Vanderbilt tumour profiles estimate almost no tumour cells in melanoma. I restricted the score to the melanoma reference and reran. This changed the result: Cancer vs response went from p = 0.038 (higher in non-responders) to p = 0.60.
- **Stacked composition plot:** the first version mixed compartments from different references, and "Other" took up most of each bar. I redrew it from a single reference: the melanoma scRNAseq signature, median of 4 methods.
- **Low-total sample:** `8_PD1_PRE` totals about 41k TPM, against a median of about 510k. It still has a normal number of detected genes, so I kept it and flagged it.
- **Not investigated:**
  - The R script printed 16 warnings. I only saw the one about ggplot dropping the `shape` aesthetic, which is cosmetic.
  - DeconRNASeq printed "number of cell types in the mixtures = 1" from its internal PCA.
  - One sample has a Quantiseq immune fraction of 1.0, with an uncharacterized fraction of about 0.
- **Expected discards:** total-immune features from immune-only references were dropped for low variance. This is expected, because those references only estimate immune cells, so their immune totals are always close to 1.

## 5. Checks

**Before deconvolution:**
- Value range, no NAs, no negative values, not integers, no duplicate genes.
- Per-sample totals after converting back to linear TPM.
- Number of detected genes in the low-total sample.
- All 73 samples match the clinical table.

**After deconvolution:**
- Which cell types each signature estimates.
- Which features make up each subgroup.
- Spearman agreement among the immune estimates (0.40–0.75) and among the stromal estimates.
- I viewed the stacked composition plot, the scores-by-response plot and the immune vs stromal scatter.
- I did not view the ranked immune plot or the heatmap.

**Credentials:** I searched `results/` for the CIBERSORTx token. It appears in clear text only in `01_deconvolution/manifest.json`. Earlier I said it was "masked" in the session log. I only confirmed that it isn't there in clear text; I didn't check whether it is masked or simply absent.

## 6. Limits

- **No ground truth:** none of the estimates are validated against measured cell fractions.
- **Relative scores:** the scores rank patients within this cohort only and can't be compared with other cohorts.
- **Absolute fractions:** these differ a lot between references (median immune fraction 0.15 to 0.65), so `*_fraction` values are rough.
- **Moderate agreement:** some pairs of immune estimates agree only weakly (ρ ≈ 0.4).
- **Arbitrary cutoffs:** the tertile and median splits are arbitrary.
- **Exploratory tests:** the response tests are exploratory. BH correction was applied within my own set of tests. This is not a predictive model.
- **Outliers:** two non-responders (7_PD1_PRE and 6_PD1_PRE) are among the most infiltrated.
- **Flagged sample:** `8_PD1_PRE` is low-quality and should be interpreted with caution.
- **My earlier description:** my description of immune-high tumours (T cells, NK cells, macrophages) came from looking at the plot, not from a formal test.
- **Credentials:** the token is still in plain text in `01_deconvolution/manifest.json`.

- My own R script, `results/scripts/04_immune_stromal_summary.R`, which computes the consensus scores, classes, Wilcoxon and Fisher tests, and figures

**Skipped:**
- `benchmark_deconvolution`: there are no known cell fractions to compare against.
- `relate_subgroups_to_pathways`: you didn't ask for it, and it needs pathway activity.
- `replicate_subgroups`: you didn't ask for a second cohort. `Riaz_log2TPM.txt` is in `data/` but I didn't use it.
- CellTFusion: infiltration is a composition question.
- BioinfoTools `scores_stat_analysis_categorical`: I did the response and therapy tests in my own R script instead. That was a choice, not a requirement.

## 3. Non-default parameters

**`run_deconvolution`:**
- `normalized=FALSE`, because the input was linear TPM.
- CBSX credentials, read from your file.
- `workers=3`, after the first run used 19 workers and ran out of memory.
- `output_dir` and `file_name`.
- I listed the methods explicitly, but they are the same five as the default.

**`aggregate_cell_groups`:** I defined the groups myself:
- Immune included mast cells and eosinophils.
- Myeloid excluded mast cells and eosinophils.
- Lymphocytes included plasma cells.

**`analyze_deconvolution`:**
- `cells_extra = Immune, Lymphocytes, Stromal`.
- `Myeloid.cells` is already standard multideconv naming, so it was kept anyway.
- I left all other parameters at their defaults. The README says "corr 0.7, Spearman"; I did not check those defaults, so treat that as unverified.

**My own script:**
- Consensus score = mean of each patient's within-cohort percentile across that compartment's features.
- Immune classes are tertiles; the immune × stromal classes use median splits.
- QC flag for samples with a TPM total below 25% of the median.
- The Cancer score uses only `Cancer_Subgroup.2`, the melanoma reference.

All of these are my own choices, not established cutoffs.

## 4. Problems

- **Out-of-memory crash:** the first `run_deconvolution` was killed (exit −9) when DWLS started on 19 workers. The machine had 15 GB RAM with about 5 GB free. I reran with 3 workers, and it completed.
- **Cancer score:** I first used all "Cancer" features. The HNSCC and Vanderbilt tumour profiles estimate almost no tumour cells in melanoma. I restricted the score to the melanoma reference and reran. This changed the result: Cancer vs response went from p = 0.038 (higher in non-responders) to p = 0.60.
- **Stacked composition plot:** the first version mixed compartments from different references, and "Other" took up most of each bar. I redrew it from a single reference: the melanoma scRNAseq signature, median of 4 methods.
- **Low-total sample:** `8_PD1_PRE` totals about 41k TPM, against a median of about 510k. It still has a normal number of detected genes, so I kept it and flagged it.
- **Not investigated:**
  - The R script printed 16 warnings. I only saw the one about ggplot dropping the `shape` aesthetic, which is cosmetic.
  - DeconRNASeq printed "number of cell types in the mixtures = 1" from its internal PCA.
  - One sample has a Quantiseq immune fraction of 1.0, with an uncharacterized fraction of about 0.
- **Expected discards:** total-immune features from immune-only references were dropped for low variance. This is expected, because those references only estimate immune cells, so their immune totals are always close to 1.

## 5. Checks

**Before deconvolution:**
- Value range, no NAs, no negative values, not integers, no duplicate genes.
- Per-sample totals after converting back to linear TPM.
- Number of detected genes in the low-total sample.
- All 73 samples match the clinical table.

**After deconvolution:**
- Which cell types each signature estimates.
- Which features make up each subgroup.
- Spearman agreement among the immune estimates (0.40–0.75) and among the stromal estimates.
- I viewed the stacked composition plot, the scores-by-response plot and the immune vs stromal scatter.
- I did not view the ranked immune plot or the heatmap.

**Credentials:** I searched `results/` for the CIBERSORTx token. It appears in clear text only in `01_deconvolution/manifest.json`. Earlier I said it was "masked" in the session log. I only confirmed that it isn't there in clear text; I didn't check whether it is masked or simply absent.

## 6. Limits

- **No ground truth:** none of the estimates are validated against measured cell fractions.
- **Relative scores:** the scores rank patients within this cohort only and can't be compared with other cohorts.
- **Absolute fractions:** these differ a lot between references (median immune fraction 0.15 to 0.65), so `*_fraction` values are rough.
- **Moderate agreement:** some pairs of immune estimates agree only weakly (ρ ≈ 0.4).
- **Arbitrary cutoffs:** the tertile and median splits are arbitrary.
- **Exploratory tests:** the response tests are exploratory. BH correction was applied within my own set of tests. This is not a predictive model.
- **Outliers:** two non-responders (7_PD1_PRE and 6_PD1_PRE) are among the most infiltrated.
- **Flagged sample:** `8_PD1_PRE` is low-quality and should be interpreted with caution.
- **My earlier description:** my description of immune-high tumours (T cells, NK cells, macrophages) came from looking at the plot, not from a formal test.
- **Credentials:** the token is still in plain text in `01_deconvolution/manifest.json`.

message:
One last step. Save copies of the results you already produced in a standard format, so that they can be compared with other analyses. Do not compute anything new, do not rerun any method and do not change any existing file: only convert what already exists. Put the files in results/standard/. If you did not produce an item, skip it and say so. If you produced several variants, export the one you presented as your main result. Tables are CSV files with one row per patient and a first column named `patient` holding the sample names exactly as in the input data.

- deconvolution_raw.csv: the deconvolution matrix as returned by the deconvolution step (all method, signature and cell-type features), before any harmonization.
- deconvolution_harmonized.csv: the matrix after harmonization into cell subgroups, if you did that step.
- subgroups_composition.csv: the composition of the subgroups of the harmonized deconvolution (the "Deconvolution subgroups composition" returned by the deconvolution analysis), one row per member, with columns subgroup (the subgroup name exactly as in deconvolution_harmonized.csv) and feature (the name of a raw deconvolution feature in that subgroup, exactly as in deconvolution_raw.csv). If a subgroup contains another subgroup, list its raw features. (Not one row per patient.)
- immune_score.csv: columns patient, immune_score (the score you used to rank patients by immune infiltration; higher = more infiltrated) and stromal_score if you computed one.
- info.json: {"input_scale": scale of the expression values given to the deconvolution ("linear TPM" or "log2"), "methods": deconvolution methods that ran, "cibersortx": true or false}.

Finish with a one-line list of the files written.

input.command:
mkdir -p results/standard && Rscript -e '
inp <- colnames(read.delim("data/Gide_log2TPM.txt", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE, nrows=2))
fix <- function(df) { p <- sub("^X", "", rownames(df)); p[!p %in% inp] <- rownames(df)[!p %in% inp]; stopifnot(all(p %in% inp), !anyDuplicated(p)); data.frame(patient=p, df, check.names=FALSE) }
raw <- read.csv("results/02_aggregated_groups/result.csv", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
d01 <- read.csv("results/01_deconvolution/result.csv", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
stopifnot(all(colnames(d01) %in% colnames(raw)))
write.csv(fix(raw), "results/standard/deconvolution_raw.csv", row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
h <- read.csv("results/03_harmonized_subgroups/result_Deconvolution.matrix.csv", row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
write.csv(fix(h), "results/standard/deconvolution_harmonized.csv", row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
r <- readRDS("results/03_harmonized_subgroups/result.rds")
comp <- r[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
flat <- list(); for (ct in names(comp)) for (sg in names(comp[[ct]])) flat[[sg]] <- comp[[ct]][[sg]]
expand <- function(f) unlist(lapply(f, function(x) if (x %in% names(flat)) expand(flat[[x]]) else x))
sc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(flat), function(sg) data.frame(subgroup=sg, feature=unique(expand(flat[[sg]])))))
cat("subgroups:", length(flat), " rows:", nrow(sc), " nested:", sum(unlist(flat) %in% names(flat)), "\n")
cat("subgroups not in harmonized:", sum(!unique(sc$subgroup) %in% colnames(h)), " features not in raw:", sum(!sc$feature %in% colnames(raw)), "\n")
cat("harmonized Subgroup cols not in composition:", sum(!grep("_Subgroup", colnames(h), value=TRUE) %in% sc$subgroup), "\n")
write.csv(sc, "results/standard/subgroups_composition.csv", row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
s <- read.csv("results/04_immune_stromal_summary/patient_immune_stromal_scores.csv", check.names=FALSE)
stopifnot(all(s$Sample %in% inp), nrow(s)==73)
write.csv(data.frame(patient=s$Sample, immune_score=s$Immune_score, stromal_score=s$Stromal_score), "results/standard/immune_score.csv", row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
meth <- unique(sub("_.*","",colnames(d01))); cat("methods in raw:", meth, "\n")
' && cat > results/standard/info.json <<'EOF'
{"input_scale": "linear TPM", "methods": ["Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS", "CBSX"], "cibersortx": true}
EOF
ls results/standard; head -3 results/standard/immune_score.csv; head -3 results/standard/subgroups_composition.csv; head -c 200 results/standard/deconvolution_harmonized.csv

content.text:
I wrote all five files to `results/standard/`. They are copies or format conversions of existing results: nothing was recomputed and no existing file was changed. Patient names match the column names of `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt` exactly (I removed the "X" prefix R had added).

- **`deconvolution_raw.csv`** (73 × 462): this is not the deconvolution output alone. I exported the matrix after `aggregate_cell_groups` (`02_aggregated_groups/result.csv`), which is what went into harmonization.
  - It contains all 375 original features from `run_deconvolution`, unchanged, plus the 87 Immune, Lymphocytes, Myeloid.cells and Stromal sums I added before harmonization.
  - I used this version because several subgroups are built from those summed features, and they need to exist in the raw file for the composition table to match. The deconvolution-only matrix is still in `results/01_deconvolution/result.csv`.
- **`deconvolution_harmonized.csv`** (73 × 222): the output of `analyze_deconvolution`.
- **`subgroups_composition.csv`**: 83 subgroups with 262 member rows.
  - No subgroup contains another subgroup.
  - Every subgroup name appears in the harmonized file, and every member feature appears in the raw file.
- **`immune_score.csv`**: the consensus immune and stromal scores I used to rank patients (mean within-cohort percentile; higher means more infiltrated).
- **`info.json`**: input scale was linear TPM; the five methods were Quantiseq, Epidish, DeconRNASeq, DWLS and CBSX; `cibersortx` is true.

Nothing requested was skipped.

Files written: `deconvolution_raw.csv`, `deconvolution_harmonized.csv`, `subgroups_composition.csv`, `immune_score.csv`, `info.json`
